title: Castaldo 1552 (catalogue 1332): Ferdinand I to G. B. Castaldo in a homophonic symbol cipher, read with a key rebuilt from the marginal decipherments of sister letters

documents.shelfmark: Milan, Biblioteca Ambrosiana, G 275 inf., unit 9, ff. 34r-35v

plaintext.source: No decipherment on this letter; the sister letters of 13, 18 and 22 Oct carry marginal decipherments.

transcription.notes: Hash sign: one-bar (l) and two-bar (o) forms not separated; d and b forms sometimes confused.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution with about 45 symbols, nulls and plain Latin decoy words; a few code signs for names and for the army

prior_solution.where: No marginal decipherment on this letter (Carpentieri 2012); catalogue 1332 open (checked 29 Oct 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: Volume G 275 inf. paged through on the Ambrosiana digital library; glossed sister letters located.
Key K1 rebuilt by automatic alignment of the glossed passages of the letters of 13 and 18 Oct with their contemporary marginal decipherments; frozen.
Held-out glossed passages of the letter of 22 Oct: f. 44v (K1) 0.918 characters / 0.731 words; f. 45v (K2) 0.932 / 0.778; 200 permuted controls at most 0.31 / 0.03.
Ff. 34r-35v (about 82 lines) transcribed, decoded with K2 and read; code sign C8 = Lippa from the gloss of f. 45v.

outcome.method_basis: Key rebuilt from contemporary marginal decipherments of sister letters in the same volume, validated on held-out glossed passages.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 316/319 words read in their sense; 273 certain (85.6%), 41 probable (12.9%), 2 restored (0.6%), 3 unresolved code groups (0.9%).

credits.note: key rebuilt from the glosses of the sister letters, validated on held-out passages; ff. 34r-35v read, English translation

texts.label: Ferdinand I to Castaldo, Vienna, 15 Oct 1552, ciphered passages ff. 34r-35v
texts.summary: Ferdinand regrets that Castaldo could not make a diversion towards Lippa to draw the Turks away from the siege of Eger and support Maurice of Saxony, accepts his excuses, announces money and cloth for the soldiers so that they do not leave, and expects the Turks to be driven from Eger by the army or the winter.
